content.comment_body: I'm interested in using [company_name] [product_name] for home automation. However, I can't find a way to connect all my pushbuttons without running individual cables for each one. I'm looking for a cost-effective method, similar to what Dobiss offers with their FTP bus and cheap bus couplers for around €5. I want to use [company_name] [product_name] but need some help to achieve this.
For the [product_name] [article_no], there is a KNX module available, but it's not exactly inexpensive. I'm not aware of any other bus system that could serve this purpose.
Thank you for your response. Unfortunately, KNX isn't affordable; each pushbutton costs about €40.
I discovered a DIY bus system at [url] where, using a standard UTP cable, numerous diodes, and seven digital inputs of your [product_name], it's possible to achieve 64 pushbutton combinations.
That looks great, thanks for sharing.

analysis.insight_summary: Users interested in home automation with [product_name] are searching for cost-effective ways to connect multiple push buttons. Existing [company_name]-compatible solutions like KNX modules are too expensive, especially compared to competitor options that offer similar features at a much lower price. Forum suggestions include creative, DIY approaches outside of [company_name], emphasizing the lack of affordable input bus choices for [product_name].
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy and affordable way to connect multiple push buttons to [product_name], similar to competitors' low-cost bus-coupling systems.
